title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: The ICSP Programme, implemented by Trócaire in the Nyamagabe, Nyaruguru and Rulindo regions of Rwanda, contributes to outcome 2.1 Poor and marginalised people, especially women and youth, have sustainable lives including diverse food sources and economic wellbeing. The objective is to engage communities in protecting and enhancing biodiversity/natural resources and the environment. Activities include training and awareness raising; supporting community-led natural resource governance and disaster risk management processes; alongside supporting the implementation of these governance and disaster risk reduction action plans. The programme is in partnership with Caritas Gikongoro, Duhamic-ADRI, UNICOOPAGI, RCCDN, RDO and BIOCOOR. Trócaire Rwanda will also support partners in their emergency preparedness planning. ---- The principal focus of this outcome is:• Community-led management of natural resources to protect local landscapes, habitats and wild biodiversity and strengthen the resilience of communities to the ongoing impacts of climate change including the implementation of Community Environment and Climate Change Action Plans.• Integrated community-led disaster risk management processes to protect and strengthen communities’ abilities to face crises and also to protect and enhance the natural and other assets they have.• Natural resource management is directly linked to climate adaptation as many of the impacts of climate are closely connected to changes in natural ecosystems e.g. land, water, soil, air.• Rural Women and youth farmers, pastoralists and natural resources users. Capacity strengthening of communities is a core element of the approach leading to stronger community structures e.g. Village Natural Resources Management Committees in which women gain leadership roles.
